title: Segmentation
description: Groups of customers (or items, or places) that behave alike, when there is no outcome to predict.
reliability: stability interval per number of segments
density view and its noise share
question: Which decisions does DCLab reach on a segmentation problem (Groups of customers (or items, or places) that behave alike, when there is no outcome to predict), and do they hold?
hypothesis: Each decision a careful data scientist reaches on this kind of problem holds on every seed of the kind's replica.
setup_summary: The segmentation kind's replica on seeds 0, 1, 2, brought as a person would; its own machine in dclab_core solve it, and each decision is checked on the finished run. No model is called.

claims.statement: Segmentation: on 3 of 3 seeds every decision held (95% interval over seeds [0.439, 1.0]); 18 of 18 decision checks held.
limitations: Invented replicas with planted traps, three seeds: what the kind decides, not how well it does on real data.
Checks on one seed share its data, so they are not independent: the interval over seeds is the honest one.
The engine does not run this kind yet: it runs as a library (dclab_core).
